From c6cecc4b9324b97775d7002a13460c247f586e8e Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Sean Christopherson <seanjc@google.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2021 23:56:15 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] KVM: x86/mmu: Complete prefetch for trailing SPTEs for
 direct, legacy MMU

Make a final call to direct_pte_prefetch_many() if there are "trailing"
SPTEs to prefetch, i.e. SPTEs for GFNs following the faulting GFN.  The
call to direct_pte_prefetch_many() in the loop only handles the case
where there are !PRESENT SPTEs preceding a PRESENT SPTE.

E.g. if the faulting GFN is a multiple of 8 (the prefetch size) and all
SPTEs for the following GFNs are !PRESENT, the loop will terminate with
"start = sptep+1" and not prefetch any SPTEs.

Prefetching trailing SPTEs as intended can drastically reduce the number
of guest page faults, e.g. accessing the first byte of every 4kb page in
a 6gb chunk of virtual memory, in a VM with 8gb of preallocated memory,
the number of pf_fixed events observed in L0 drops from ~1.75M to <0.27M.

Note, this only affects memory that is backed by 4kb pages as KVM doesn't
prefetch when installing hugepages.  Shadow paging prefetching is not
affected as it does not batch the prefetches due to the need to process
the corresponding guest PTE.  The TDP MMU is not affected because it
doesn't have prefetching, yet...

Fixes: 957ed9effd80 ("KVM: MMU: prefetch ptes when intercepted guest #PF")
Cc: Sergey Senozhatsky <senozhatsky@google.com>
Cc: Ben Gardon <bgardon@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Sean Christopherson <seanjc@google.com>
Message-Id: <20210818235615.2047588-1-seanjc@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>

diff --git a/arch/x86/kvm/mmu/mmu.c b/arch/x86/kvm/mmu/mmu.c
index 1a64ba5b9437..4238fe3e91c2 100644
--- a/arch/x86/kvm/mmu/mmu.c
+++ b/arch/x86/kvm/mmu/mmu.c
@@ -2842,11 +2842,13 @@ static void __direct_pte_prefetch(struct kvm_vcpu *vcpu,
 			if (!start)
 				continue;
 			if (direct_pte_prefetch_many(vcpu, sp, start, spte) < 0)
-				break;
+				return;
 			start = NULL;
 		} else if (!start)
 			start = spte;
 	}
+	if (start)
+		direct_pte_prefetch_many(vcpu, sp, start, spte);
 }
 
 static void direct_pte_prefetch(struct kvm_vcpu *vcpu, u64 *sptep)
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/x86/kvm/mmu/mmu.c`**
   - A new conditional check was added after the loop in the `__direct_pte_prefetch` function. If the variable `start` is not NULL (indicating there are trailing SPTEs to prefetch), it calls `direct_pte_prefetch_many(vcpu, sp, start, spte)`. This ensures that any trailing SPTEs following the faulting GFN are prefetched, which was not handled in the previous implementation.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `mmu.c` directly addresses a bug related to the handling of SPTEs (Shadow Page Table Entries) during page fault handling in the KVM (Kernel-based Virtual Machine) module. The added logic ensures that not only the preceding SPTEs are prefetched but also any trailing SPTEs that may not have been prefetched due to the loop's termination condition. This change is intended to improve performance by reducing the number of guest page faults, particularly in scenarios where multiple SPTEs are not present. The fix is linked to a previous commit that introduced the prefetching mechanism, indicating that this modification is a corrective measure to enhance the functionality introduced earlier.

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the failure to prefetch trailing SPTEs for GFNs that follow the faulting GFN when all preceding SPTEs were not present. The loop in the `__direct_pte_prefetch` function only handled the case for preceding SPTEs, leading to missed prefetching of necessary SPTEs, which could result in an increased number of guest page faults.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void __direct_pte_prefetch(struct kvm_vcpu *vcpu,
 				  struct kvm_mmu_page *sp, u64 *sptep)
 {
 	u64 *spte, *start = NULL;
 	int i;
 
 	WARN_ON(!sp->role.direct);
 
 	i = (sptep - sp->spt) & ~(PTE_PREFETCH_NUM - 1);
 	spte = sp->spt + i;
 
 	for (i = 0; i < PTE_PREFETCH_NUM; i++, spte++) {
 		if (is_shadow_present_pte(*spte) || spte == sptep) {
 			if (!start)
 				continue;
 			if (direct_pte_prefetch_many(vcpu, sp, start, spte) < 0)
-				break;
+				return;
 			start = NULL;
 		} else if (!start)
 			start = spte;
 	}
+	if (start)
+		direct_pte_prefetch_many(vcpu, sp, start, spte);
 }

The logic within the loop only addresses the case for present SPTEs and does not ensure that trailing SPTEs are prefetched if `start` is set. Therefore, it fails to address the root cause of the bug.

Reason: The provided code snippet still contains the bug because it does not handle the case where all preceding SPTEs are not present. The loop only prefetches SPTEs when it encounters a present SPTE or the specific SPTE being checked (`sptep`). If all preceding SPTEs are absent, the `start` variable will not be set, and the trailing SPTEs will not be prefetched, leading to potential missed prefetching and increased guest page faults. The fix that was supposed to be applied (the call to `direct_pte_prefetch_many()` after the loop) is present, but it does not address the root cause of the bug in the loop logic itself.
